target_subject: astronomical clock with surrounding sculptural figures

scene: A large ornate astronomical clock mounted on a stone facade with multiple sculptural figures above and beside it
Two rectangular windows flank a central statue; each window contains at least one visible human-like figure
A skeletal figure holding an hourglass stands to the right of the clock face
action: The clock hands indicate approximately 10:10, with a separate inner dial showing a different time or celestial position
Figures in the left window appear static, with one holding a golden object; figures in the right window are partially obscured but present
The central seated figure holds an open book and gazes upward, while the skeleton holds an hourglass upright
rationale: The presence of Roman numerals, zodiac symbols, and multiple concentric dials suggests an astronomical function rather than a simple timepiece
The skeleton holding an hourglass is a conventional memento mori motif, implying thematic reference to mortality
The unreadable text on the outer ring (e.g., 'APRILIS', 'MAY') appears to be Latin month names, supporting calendrical functionality
object: The clock face has three concentric rings: outer ring with Roman numerals I–XII and Latin month abbreviations, middle ring with zodiac symbols and Arabic numerals 1–24, inner ring with astrological glyphs and a sun pointer.
Above the clock, a seated stone figure holds an open book and looks upward; flanking this figure are two recessed windows each containing at least one human-like sculpted figure.
To the right of the clock, a standing skeletal figure holds an hourglass in its left hand and a scroll or tablet in its right hand.
Below the central statue, two small animal-like sculptures (possibly lions or dogs) rest on the ledge.
A golden rooster or bird sculpture sits atop a niche directly above the central statue.

symbolic_mapping: skeleton and hourglass map to transience of life
sun pointer on zodiac ring maps to cyclical inevitability
philosophy_interpretations.interpretation: The juxtaposition of mechanical timekeeping with the skeletal memento mori visually enacts the philosophical tension between measured duration and finite existence.
alternative_interpretations: The skeleton may represent a specific allegorical figure (e.g., Chronos or Death) in a civic or religious tableau, not necessarily a universal philosophical statement.
limitations: No inscriptions confirm intended meaning; the skeleton’s pose and attributes are generic across European medieval iconography.

visual_anchors: central seated figure with open book
symbolic_mapping: open book maps to recorded knowledge
window figures map to witnesses or authorities
philosophy_interpretations.interpretation: The arrangement implies that truth is mediated through authoritative figures and textual tradition, with time serving as the framework within which knowledge is validated.
alternative_interpretations: The figures may simply represent saints or patrons associated with the building, without epistemological intent.
limitations: The book’s content is invisible; facial expressions and gestures are stylized and non-indicative of cognitive states.

symbolic_mapping: layered dials map to hierarchical order of cosmos
animals map to earthly realm beneath celestial mechanics
philosophy_interpretations.interpretation: The stratified design reflects a pre-modern cosmology where human society is positioned within a fixed, multi-layered order governed by celestial cycles and symbolic guardianship.
alternative_interpretations: The layout follows standard astronomical clock conventions for displaying sidereal, solar, and calendar time—functional, not sociological.
limitations: No human figures are shown engaging with the clock; social roles are inferred solely from iconographic convention.
